title: A log timestamp, letter by letter

blocks.text: Every line of a service's log starts with a timestamp such as `2024-03-15 14:30:45`. Write `LogStamp.format(LocalDateTime t)`, which prints `t` that way:

items: the four-digit year, the month and the day of the month, joined by `-`;
the hour, the minute and the second, joined by `:`;
every field but the year padded to two digits;
no fraction of a second, even when `t` has one.

blocks.text: The hour is on the **24-hour clock** (`14`, and `00` just after midnight), and the year is the **calendar year** of the date, on every day of the year.

cases.says: A morning entry prints as year-month-day, then hours, minutes and seconds, each padded to two digits.
July at 09:41 prints month 07 and minute 41.
14:30 prints as 14, and a quarter past midnight as 00.
December 30 and 31, 2024 print with the year 2024.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Pattern letters are case-sensitive: MM is the month and mm the minute, HH the 24-hour hour and hh the 12-hour one, and a doubled letter pads to two digits.
